This, in order to follow the rules and conditions that apply to the employees in the workplace. This framework determines the employment relation laws and regulations showing the responsibilities, activities, and rights of the parties.

  • Employment contracts in the UAE must follow all the labor laws which are set by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE). Carefully considering the interests of both the employers and employees and ensuring a fair treatment for all the employees in the workplace.
  • Usually, in the UAE labor contracts contain a lot of information. Such as workers responsibilities and job duties, schedule of the employees during the working day, salary and benefits. Also, a list of leaves that employee is entitled to, employment probation period, termination procedures and ways to resolve possible disputes.
  • Authorities required employers to provide the written job contracts to all workers who were hired. This is regardless of the citizenship or the job position.
  • The contracts must be drawn up in Arabic or bilingual. With Arabic being the language that is mainly used, and must be in accordance with the relevant legislation related to the UAE labor regulations.

Examining the employment contracts of the UAE must be essential for both employers and employees. As a method to ensure compliance with the law and to safeguard their interests and rights in the workplace. The consequences of breaking the labor law may include fines, penalties, and, in cases, lawsuits.

Therefore, it is essential for both parties to familiarize themselves with the provisions of the employment contract. Moreover, we suggest to seek legal advice if needed to ensure a fair and transparent employment relationship.

Types of Employment Contracts UAE

It is essential for employers and employees to know the different employment contracts in the UAE. There are several important reasons that should be in the top of our list.

  • Legal Compliance: Commitment to the fairness and equal employment policies regarding contracts guarantees for the legal compliance with the UAE labor laws. There are specific types of contracts that can be different for various industries or job roles which makes following regulations of these jobs a must to stay away from litigations and penalties.
  • Employee Rights and Protections: If people are knowledgeable about the nuances between being on a fixed term contract and an unlimited term contract they can be aware of their rights and their protection when on each of these kinds of agreements.
  • Job Stability and Security: Learning the nature of employment contract enables workers to understand the degree of job stability as well as security they have.
  • Planning and Forecasting: Workers can make decisions based on whether the type of contract offered is permanent, contractual or permit-based and employers can do their workforce management at their convenience.
  • Dispute Resolution: The transparency that arises from knowing the essence of contracts in terms of duties and rights lets management resolve negotiations and lawsuits easier.
  • Economic Implications: For instance, unlimited term contracts can make it possible to have a higher stability level but at the same time it can be relatively costly for the employer, being evident in the benefits costs and in the employee’s severance pay.

Fundamentally, the knowledge on the category of employment contracts among UAE is a key matter. Therefore, to promote fair and transparent employment relationships. Observing the legal compliance and facilitate good workplace administration from two sides of employer and employee.

Limited Term Contract (Fixed Term Contract)

Under the Limited Term Contract, the employer and the employee set out a period of employment for which the employee will be working. This period is usually how long their services will last. A start and finish dates will be set in the contract with the outline of their duration.

Many LTCs involve a fixed employment time span. Which depends on the duration of the job and the mutual agreement between the parties. This period may range from one year to five years.

  • Specific End Date: On the other part to UnLimited Term Contracts, Limited Term Contracts specified end date is clear after this date, the job is complete and the relationship breaks unless it is renewed or extended.
  • Renewal Clause: Such contracts could also include clauses about renewal or extension of service period upon an agreement from the employer and the employee. Nevertheless, renewals are not automatic and open to debate.
  • Termination Restrictions: Workers on Limited Term Contracts may also have strictly defined contractual terms on ending their contract before the contract end date, which shall rule by contractual terms or UAE labor law.
  • Implications: Whilst Limited Term Contracts provide a well-defined timeframe as regards the employment period, limited security may be created compared to Unlimited Term Contracts in the same situation.

Labour laws and regulations in UAE should be well understood by workers in these categories. They should be granting end-of-service benefits like other masses of workers as stipulated in the legislation.

Unlimited Term Contract (Open Ended Contract)

An unlimited term contract in the UAE is a type of employment agreement which does not have a definite expiry date. Rather continues endlessly until it is brought to an end by either the employer or the employee, depending on the provisions of the UAE labor law.

This contract does not tie with a specific period for employment. Thus, providing a bigger flexibility and certainty for the employees and the employers.

  • Indefinite Duration: Open-end Term Contracts remain valid for an unlimited period of time without a binding termination date set, as long as an employee was not detached according to law.
  • Termination Flexibility: Workers in Unlimited Term Contracts frequently enjoy higher flexibility of employment conditions, which may usually include notice requirements and other termination conditions either defined in the contract or labor law.
  • Continuous Renewal: Contrary to Limited Term, these contracts are not subject to periodic extension, they intend to remain operational until either party communicates notice to terminate the employment relationship.
  • Implications: Employees working under Unlimited Term Contracts (UTC) have long-term job security as their employment will be ongoing without fear or worry of contract renewal. Employers, on the other hand, bear in mind that there may be some long-term commitments for these contracts and the responsibilities under UAE labor laws they include.

What is the new Labor Law in UAE 2025?

The UAE has adopted a number of important changes and policies. It has enacted a new UAE labor law, updated its Emiratisation law, introduced an unemployment insurance program, and regulations for fixed-term agreements.

The latest law may comprise of the modification of the existing labor regulations. Also, measures to support a favorable work atmosphere according to the internationally acceptable standards:

Emiratisation Policy:

  • The Emiratisation policy is a strategic project implemented to boost the involvement or participation of all Emirati workers across various domains of the economy.
  • The Emirati policy can suffer modifications to include other targets, incentives and support. Intended to boost the percentage of Emirati citizens working in the private sector, the private sector companies will hire and train Emiratis.

Unemployment Insurance Plan:

  • The development of an unemployment insurance plan reflects a progressive attitude on the part of the UAE government in taking steps for the resolution of unemployment challenges and provision of a security belt for workers who lose their jobs.
  • These measures may provide financial aid and assistance services to individuals with no choice of unemployment, thus guiding them through periods of job transition as well as moments of economic uncertainty.

Provision for Fixed-Term Contracts:

  • Now, all labor contracts should be of fixed duration. Under the revised labor law, employers and employees can enter into predetermined duration agreements which determine the employment period.
  • The fixed-term employment follows the pattern of flexibility for employers. Whether the project is short-term or seasonal for employees this is the aspect of the matter of the period of their employment.

Adjustments to Work Modes:

  • With the aim of facilitating remote work, flexible work hours, job-sharing, and arrangements. This is changing as the labor market evolves fast.

Key Aspects of UAE Labour Law

Understanding these key aspects is of high importance for every employer as well as for every employee. To make sure they meet all the law requirements and their rights in the workplace are respected. Here are some of the key aspects of the UAE Labour Law:

  1. Employment Contracts
  2. Working Hours and Rest Periods
  3. Wages and Benefits
  4. Health and Safety Standards
  5. Termination Procedures

Employee Rights and Benefits

  • Minimum Wage: Employees in the UAE are guaranteed to receive a minimum wage which is set by the government. However, this amount may be different from one industry to the next and may also depend on the job qualification of the individual.
  • Working Hours: The employees have the right to work for a particular amount of hours per week. Generally, not more than 48 hours every week, with the additional amounts paid as overtime fee for the extra working hours.
  • Leave Entitlements: The labor law of the UAE affords employees such benefits of leaves. This includes annual leave, sick leave, maternity leave, and public holidays, among others.
  • End-of-Service Benefits: Employees who have completed their term of employment are eligible to gratuity, a benefit referred to as end-of-service benefits. Gratuity depends on the service length and the salary of the flat of last salary.
  • Healthcare and Insurance: Employers have to give healthcare opportunities and insurance benefits to their employees, such as pre-hospitalization expenses and work related injuries.
  • Protection from Discrimination and Harassment: Workers have the right to work in a system where he or she is free from discrimination, abuse and disrespect along racial or country of origin, religion or disability lines.

Employer Obligations and Regulations

  • Providing Employment Contracts: Written employment contracts needs to be offered to all workers by employers, explaining employee rights and responsibilities, as is laid down in UAE labour law.
  • Payment of Wages: Workers should be paid by their employers their wages always on time, mostly at the end of every month, and in accordance with the conditions specified in the work contract.
  • Ensuring Workplace Safety: An employer must ensure that employees can work in a healthy and safe environment that has been carefully designed bearing in mind the safety procedures, staff training and health and safety regulations.
  • Compliance with Labor Laws: The responsible employers must observe all the labor laws and regulations, those of employment contracts, hours of work, leave entitlements and dismissals.
  • Respecting Employee Rights: Employers should give employees the required rights, for example, their right to privacy, association, and discrimination as well as harassment protection.
  • Providing End-of-Service Benefits: When employees reach the end of the service with employers, employers are liable to calculate and give them their end-of-service benefits such as gratuity which are set out in the UAE labor law.

Specific Employment Scenarios

  • Termination of Employment: Certain procedures and criteria underpin the termination of employment contracts in UAE, consisting of notice period, reasons of termination, and benefits on departure, which are called end-of-service benefits.
  • Workplace Disputes: In the case of the conflicting types of the employer and employees, the specific mechanisms are involved, such as mediation, and arbitration or the dispute resolution in labour courts, for remedy of the issue and the claims.
  • Employment of Foreign Nationals: Employing foreign nationals entails compliance with immigration and residency regulations which include providing a working permit and visa to employees.
  • Maternity and Parental Leave: UAE labor law includes stipulations regarding maternity and parental leave as part of the benefit system for female employees in terms of leave before and after childbirth and also paternity leave for male employees.
  • Redundancy and Layoffs: Employers should strictly follow a certain set of actions while making redundancies or layoffs. For instance, they should provide the affected employees with a notice period, offer alternative employment options and give compensation.

It is important to know the ways in which these particular employment scenarios are performed. For the sake of both employers and employees.

Employers should take their responsibilities regarding their employees and their employees’ rights into account and consider various employment situations. Furthermore, the workers must also know the security aspects at work and the labor rights they are to acquire under the UAE labor law.

Final Words

The UAE labour law ensures an adequate and impartial working environment that is suitable to both employers and employees according to the law. The law provides a basement for employee rights with clauses of job security, set benefits, minimum wage and a safe working environment.

Employers get reassurance and have less legal risk involved by abiding to these regulations as well as that they can attract top-skilled talent with their business.

Being familiar with the legalities that govern employers’ and employees’ rights and duties under the UAE Labour Law is pivotal and key to thriving in the workplace legally. Seeking advice from legal experts becomes very helpful when it comes to clarifying some particular employment scenarios.

Through adherence to the provisions of the UAE Labour Law, employers and employees have the opportunity to develop arrangements which will lead to a more beneficial and positive working atmosphere in the UAE.

FAQs:

What is the UAE Labour Law and who does it apply to?

The UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021) governs employment relations for most private sector employees in the UAE, excluding domestic workers, DIFC/ADGM employees, and government employees covered under separate laws.

What are the standard working hours under UAE Labour Law?

The standard work hours are 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week, except for certain industries where it may vary. During Ramadan, working hours are reduced by 2 hours daily.

What types of employment contracts are allowed under UAE Labour Law?

Since 2022, only fixed-term contracts (renewable for any duration) are permitted. Unlimited contracts have been phased out.

What is the probation period for employees?

Probation cannot exceed 6 months. Employers must give 14 days’ notice to terminate during probation, and employees must give 30–90 days depending on their reason for resignation.

How is annual leave calculated in the UAE?

Employees are entitled to 30 calendar days of paid annual leave after completing one year of service. Pro-rated leave applies for employees with less than a year.

What are the rules for sick leave under the UAE Labour Law?

Employees are eligible for 90 days of sick leave per year—first 15 days fully paid, next 30 days half-paid, and the remaining 45 days unpaid.

Employee Outsourcing In Healthcare 2025: An Ultimate Guide

Employee outsourcing in healthcare in the UAE is going through a significant change that establishing itself as a vital approach in this dynamic market. Healthcare providers, including hospitals, clinics, and medical facilities are increasingly turning to outsourcing to improve operations and maintain a competitive advantage, because of increasing costs and technological developments. Meanwhile, rising demand for superior healthcare services is accelerating this trend.

In this blog, we investigate the steadily developing of outsourced medical services in 2025. We will share its benefits, contemplations, and the most recent patterns forming this practice and you will figure out how outsourcing functions inside your medical services association lead to cost savings, improved efficiency, and, better patient care.

What do you mean by employee outsourcing in healthcare?

In healthcare, employee outsourcing refers to contracting with external companies or individuals to provide specific services. Traditionally, those services are performed by in-house staff. From administrative tasks like medical billing and coding to specialized clinical functions like radiology or physiotherapy? These services have a vast range

Healthcare organizations aim to achieve greater efficiency by outsourcing functions. They also aid them in reducing operational costs. While it gains them access to a wider talent pool with specialized expertise. It allows them to hire the right talent stress-free

Importance of healthcare outsourcing in UAE

The healthcare sector of the UAE is experiencing rapid growth. However, it also faces challenges. It manages costs and attracts skilled professionals. Employee outsourcing in healthcare offers a compelling solution for healthcare institutions.

The healthcare sector can reduce costs by outsourcing non-core functions. This includes medical billing or IT services. This frees up internal resources. Potentially, it reduces overall operational expenditure.

On the other hand, outsourcing employees aid healthcare providers in accessing specialized talent. They do so by outsourcing specialized tasks. This includes physiotherapy or radiology analysis. It allows hospitals to connect with a wider talent pool while addressing challenges in recruitment. At the same time, ensuring access to the latest expertise – even without the burden of full-time recruitment and retention.

Outsourcing employees also aids healthcare departments in improving efficiency. Outsourcing frees up in-house staff to focus on core patient care activities. This leads to increased efficiency and improved patient satisfaction.

In short, the healthcare sectors have a good option to focus on growth. They can delegate non-core tasks. They can dedicate more resources to strategic initiatives and expansion plans.

Types Of Healthcare Process Outsourcing

As we all know there are many types of healthcare process outsourcing are there. The major types of healthcare process outsourcing have been discussed in detail:

Medical coding and billing

Accurate coding translates procedures into universal medical codes for insurance reimbursement. Employee outsourcing in healthcare ensures proper coding. On the other hand, they also assist in timely billing for efficient revenue cycle management.

Claims management and processing

By outsourcing specialists, healthcare can handle claim submissions, denials, and appeals to insurance companies. This ensures proper reimbursement while minimizing revenue leakage.

Data entry services

Healthcare generates vast amounts of patient data. This required skilled staff to handle this huge data. So, outsourcing data entry tasks such as appointment scheduling or insurance verification frees up internal staff. They will be available for higher-value activities instead of routine tasks

Medical record transcription

To convert dictated medical reports into electronic records is crucial for accurate patient care and record-keeping. However, outsourcing ensures timely and accurate transcription by qualified professionals.

Customer service

Excellent patient communication is vital in every field. By outsourcing call centers or chat support, health care can have extended hours or multilingual support. It enhances the patient experience.

Also Recommended: Types of Outsourcing Services

Key challenges facing healthcare providers

Here, we share the key challenges that healthcare providers face:

Workforce shortages and burnout

The healthcare industry faces a global shortage of skilled professionals. This leads to overworked staff and potential burnout. It’s the biggest challenge and compromises patient care quality.

Financial pressures

Another problem they face is rising medical services costs and stale repayments. It overburdens medical services suppliers. The medical services need to track down creative ways of overseeing costs while keeping up with quality considerations.

Technological disruption

Healthcare technology advancements necessitate continuous adaptation. But, integrating new technologies can be costly and require staff training. It’s a gap that healthcare needs to fix

Patient expectations

Patients are expected to be informed with personalized care. It allows convenient access and clear communication. To meet these evolving expectations can be challenging for healthcare providers.

Benefits of Outsourcing in Healthcare

There are several benefits of employee outsourcing in healthcare. Let’s discuss them in detail to increase your knowledge

Cost Savings

Employee outsourcing in healthcare frees up internal resources from day-to-day tasks. It reduces operational costs associated with recruitment, training, and infrastructure for specific tasks.

Access to a Wider Talent Pool

In the UAE, healthcare facilities can tap into a global specialized talent pool. This ensures access to the latest expertise without geographical limitations.

Improved Efficiency and Productivity

By delegating non-core functions to a third party, in-house staff can focus on core patient care activities. It leads to faster turnaround times and improved overall productivity.

Enhanced Expertise

Outsourcing partners specialize in specific healthcare tasks. It brings a deeper level of expertise than in-house staff. The company employee might possess those specific functions.

Focus on Patient Care

By delegating administrative tasks, healthcare providers can dedicate more resources to patient engagement, improved service delivery, and overall patient care quality.

What Can Be Outsourced in Healthcare?

A range of functions within a healthcare organization can be outsourced. It depends on the specific needs and resources available.

Administrative tasks are efficiently handled by outsourcing specialists. Repetitive tasks like medical billing and coding, appointment scheduling, insurance verification, and data entry. They all can be handled and managed smoothly

For specialized clinical needs outsourcing employees is a good option. Tasks like radiology interpretation, physiotherapy, or remote patient monitoring can be outsourced to qualified professionals.

Additionally, IT infrastructure management, software support, and data security can be outsourced. Ensuring smooth technological operations without the burden of maintaining an in-house IT department.

The non-clinical support can be outsourced also. This entails functions like housekeeping, security, or laundry services. This frees up internal staff to focus on core healthcare activities.

Employee outsourcing in healthcare involves hiring staff through a third-party outsourcing company instead of employing them directly. The outsourcing firm handles recruitment, payroll, visas, compliance, and HR operations.

Why do healthcare facilities outsource employees?

Healthcare organizations outsource to reduce operational costs, fill urgent medical staffing needs, ensure regulatory compliance, and focus on core patient care services.

What types of healthcare roles can be outsourced?

Common outsourced roles include nurses, medical technicians, lab staff, administrative staff, customer service, medical coders, pharmacists, paramedics, and support staff.

Is outsourcing in healthcare compliant with UAE regulations?

Yes. Outsourcing must comply with UAE Labour Law and MOHRE guidelines. Reputable outsourcing companies provide staff with valid work permits, visas, and insurance as per legal standards.

How does outsourcing help with staff shortages in hospitals?

Outsourcing allows hospitals and clinics to quickly onboard pre-vetted and licensed professionals, helping fill urgent shortages without long recruitment cycles.

title: HR Outsourcing: A Complete Guide to Get It Right
content:
HR Outsourcing: The Complete Guide to Success [Updated]

Outsourcing HR and administrative roles is an effective approach to obtain maximum work potential and business productivity. HR outsourcing is an efficient and strategic move for enterprises to save time and resources and concentrate on primary business operations to achieve business objectives for potential growth and success. Business entities can acquire more improved candidate experience, access a specialized skilled workforce, and save costs and resources to maximize profits and overall business activities.

In this article, we will cover HR outsourcing’s role in detail with pros and cons along with how it can be useful for businesses to achieve and improve more success.

What is HR (Human Resources) Outsourcing Services?

HR outsourcing is a service that offers HR management for other businesses on their behalf with legal compliance. title: Annual Leave In UAE: A Complete Guide
content:
What Is Annual Leave In UAE 2025? A Complete Guide

Annual leave in UAE emerges as the most significant benefit grant to workers who are provided with time off to recover. In UAE, the workers are eligible for many paid annual leave every year. However, understanding what time off you are entitled to and how to take this leave optimally is essential.

In this article, we will explain the details of the application for annual leave and see what it gives to employees. We will discuss how much leave you are entitled to, the formula to calculate it, and some useful tips to boost your time off. In addition, we will also look at the types as well as the UAE Labor Law for annual leave.

What Is Annual Leave In UAE?

Annual leave in UAE is a mandatory benefit for the employees granted by the Labor Law. This benefit allows them to relax and recharge energy. Consequently, it is a legal right that must be granted to employees by the employers.

The UAE labor law determines the minimum days of annual leave for an employee. The organization bases the days on the years of service contributed by him or her. Therefore, a longer duration with the same employer entitles an employee to more days of leave.

Furthermore, you can use this vacation leave in one continuous period or divide it into several shorter periods. This depends on an arrangement between the employer and the employee. As a result, this flexibility means that employees can take their time off whenever it is convenient both in the private and professional aspects.

  • The Federal Decree-Law No. (33) ensures that workers who have completed a year of services are granted a paid 30 days annual leave. This is mandatory.
  • Employees who complete six months to one year are granted with two days of paid leave per month.
  • Yet, it is worth mentioning that this is the minimum legal requirement. Some organizations allocate more extensive annual leave to their employees in the UAE. Some employers may offer more additional benefits such as sick leave and personal leave to their leaves.

New Labour Law Rules of Annual Leave UAE

The new UAE Labour Law for Annual Leave in 2024 introduced some significant changes. As a result, employees should be at least entitled to 30 days of annual leave while the minimum was 25 days prior. Another goal of this transformation is to improve work-life balance and employees’ well-being.

Without a doubt, employers have to adjust to these new policies. Violation of rules may result in penalties and fines. In addition, firms must amend their guidelines and disseminate the changes accurately to all staff members.

Now employees will have more free time for relaxation and recovery. Consequently, this should boost the motivation and increase the productivity. Nonetheless, employers need to implement adequate strategies for staff management during vacation time.

The new laws for annual leave in UAE focus on particular employees’ rights. These rules guarantee that all laborers in the UAE get their paid vacation days annually.

  • Each employee gets at least 30 days of paid vacation after working for a year. It applies to all workers, irrespective of their position in the organization.
  • Accrual and Carry-over. Throughout the year as they work, employees earn their annual leave entitlement. However, as distinct from the preceding regulation, normal days off cannot be transferred from one year to the next. The employer’s authorization is necessary for exceptional situations.

Also, if it was accumulated in a year, the employment comes to an end.

  • Additional Points. Employees who complete six months but less than one year of continuous service are awarded with two days of paid leave for each month they have worked. It is worth mentioning that these are just the minimum criteria. Employers can better their leave policies by inserting them in their employment contracts.

Annual Leave Policies in the UAE 

The annual leave UAE Labor Law has policies set by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation.  In the United Arab Emirates, most companies follow leave policies that allow workers to request paid time off during their annual leave.

Annual leave UAE labor law grants rather generous vacation time (paid annual leave) to all its workers:

  • Minimum entitlement. All employees who have spent a year on the job have the legal right to a minimum holiday leave of 30 days. That is the request by UAE Labour Law in Dubai.
  • Pro-rated leave. Workers who have worked with an organization for less than one year may take two half-working days off per month after the completion of six months of service.
  • Additional leave. Employees who have been with the organization for more than 4 years shall enjoy an additional 6 days of annual leave which puts them on a total of 36 days.
  • Furthermore, you must bear in mind the fact that these are the minimal legal requirements. Many companies in the UAE are a bit more tolerant when it comes to employees’ annual leave.

However, though, employers may give more than just the leave benefit to you, like sick days, compassionate days, and maternity leave.

Thus, employers leave policy can always vary. For this reason, it is always reasonable to check with your company to know exactly what is the policy in your case.

Types of Leaves in the UAE 

Paid Leaves

The United Arab Emirates provides employees some allowances to balance between work and life and hence maintain the well-being of their lives.

  • Annual Leave in UAE. employees having a year service record are granted 30 days of leave allowance. Which is well deserved for them to come back fresh and to have more quality time with their loved ones.

Please note that to request an annual leave in UAE you must first issue a letter for annual leave Besides, you should check the annual leave calculator.

  • Sick Leave: If health issues are prompting the absence of employees from their jobs. The UAE gives them 15 days of paid leave annually upon the completion of the probation period. It empowers them to set their priorities and overcome financial worries, which is important for their well-being.
  • Maternity Leave: This is a great incentive for mothers to continue with their careers since the UAE provides them with maternity leave in UAE for 45 paid leaves. Besides, one can have 45 days of unpaid leave for illness resulting from pregnancy as well. Which means that the employer is providing comprehensive support to pregnant workers.
  • Paternity Leave: Fathers hold the right to receive five paid vacation days following their child’s birth as per the law for paternity leave in UAE.
  • Compassionate Leave: Employees work and receive 5 days of compassionate leave if a close family member dies.

Annual Leave

Annual leave in UAE is a paid leave and also a legal right for all employees in the United Arab Emirates.

  • The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization stipulates that employees who have been with the company for one year can be provided with paid annual leave that should not be less than 30 days.
  • Employees who have worked for the organization for less than one year may also be eligible to earn some paid annual leave. They accumulate 2 days leave for each month of service to the maximum of 24 days. It should be mentioned that some employers in the UAE may have more liberal leave policies compared to the statutory minimum.
  • In addition to annual leave, the employees in UAE are also entitled to several public holidays that are paid off. These public holidays are not included in the annual leave and are also paid holidays. This means most of the employees in the UAE spend a generous amount of paid time off every year.

Sick Leave

In the case of the UAE, sick leave is one of the available paid benefits for workers. This leave is grant to employees depending on their contract of employment and the particular employer. Even though there are some legal requirements, it still is of little importance.

  • The UAE Labour law creates the minimum title for 15 days paid leave per year. This occurs only after a deferred employee has finished on his/her probation at a given employment. Throughout this initial 15-day period the full salary will be paid to them.
  • During the procurement of next 30 days of sick leave, employees will receive the half of the salary. Nevertheless, one must acknowledge that going beyond the 45 day period of sanctioned unauthorized leave will result to unpaid leave.

Therefore, the employer may not be under obligation, in such cases, to pay the price of the extra days which had been taken by the employee to his/her sickness.

Hence, the employees should have the knowledge of what their sick leave allowance give them according to the contract they have entered into after understanding.

Collaborating with their HR Department is especially useful to get rid of any remaining queries or possibly concerns.

Maternity Leave

UAE is one of the few countries placing a great emphasis on maternity leave. This is a benefit given to female employees to support them throughout pregnancy and during the time of childbirth.

The number of weeks for the maternity leave of UAE workers is different upon each emirate and the industry. Here is a breakdown:

Federal Government:

  • Women will receive 60 days of maternity leave with their full payment.
  • This furlough may start up to 30 days before the anticipated due date of the birth.

Dubai Government:

  • Women employees are likewise given 90 days of fully-paid maternity leave.
  • The members of the crew can file for leave not later than 30 days prior to the expected birth date.

Private Sector:

  • In line with UAEs federal law, women employed in private sector have a right to 60 days of maternity leave.
  • The first twenty two days are with full pay, and the remaining ten days are half.
  • Leave is 30 days which starts 30 days before the expected delivery.

Additional Points:

  • If a case of difficult childbirth has occurred, the employees are likely entitled to additional maternity leaves.
  • A few companies may have maternity leaves extended. Besides, other benefits aside from what is put on the statutes.

This should however be taken with caution as these are general rules and, this could vary based on the employers. You can consult the relevant legal resources and any new information you may need on the specific entitlements.

Parental Leave

Paternity leave in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) is a paid leave that allows fathers to be with their child following the deliver. This privilege belongs to both public and private sector employees-fathers.

Paternal leave duration in UAE can change according the sector of employment. Fathers engaged in public sector activities receive five days of paid leave, whereas fathers who work for private employers receive five working days of paid leave.

Fathers can use their paternal leave either in the public or private sectors and not later than six months from the birth date of the baby. This option of paternal leave cannot be taken together with other types of leave.

Compassionate Leave 

The United Arab Emirates (UAE) offers compassionate leave to employees under specific circumstances. This leave is intended to provide support during challenging personal situations, such as the death of a family member or a serious illness.

The duration of compassionate leave in the UAE is typically determined by the employer. However, as per the UAE Labour Law, employees are legally entitled to:

  • 5 days of paid leave: upon the death of a spouse.
  • 3 days of paid leave: upon the death of a parent, child, sibling, grandparent, or grandchild.

It is important to note that exceeding these mandated durations is at the employers discretion. In such cases, additional leave may be granted with or without pay, depending on the employers policies and the specific situation.

While compassionate leave is not a guaranteed right beyond the mandated durations, many employers in the UAE offer it as a form of good practice. However, It is advisable to consult your employment contract in UAE or company handbook. This will help you to understand the specific compassionate leave policy applicable to your situation.

Hajj and Umrah Leave

Hajj and Umrah denote the purposeful kind of leave that is given to employees so that they can travel to perform religion rites in Islam. Nevertheless, they have some special features in the way they are applied and their regulation.

Hajj Leave:

  • Mandatory pilgrimage. Hajj is the compulsory travel to Mecca which worthy-bodied Muslim has to perform once in his life.
  • Leave policy. Certain countries, especially in the Middle East, have the incentives by law to pay employees for those who perform Hajj in the government.
  • The private sector regulations and policies for performing Hajj mandate every airline company. This is to apply their own standards and customized legislations according to the visa granted by their country of provided transportation.

Umrah Leave:

  • Non-mandatory pilgrimage. The Umrah is a voluntary pilgrimage and it can be done at any time of the year. While in the case of the Hajj, it is obligatory to do it from the 8th of Zulhijja until the 12th of the same month.
  • No legal entitlement. There is generally no legal consideration regarding Umrah travel being compulsory in the majority of countries.
  • Leave options: Employees who wish to take part in organizing Umrah can request unpaid leave, or they can utilize their allowed annual leave.

Public Holidays

Every year, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) marks commemorative days and festivities. These holidays are about celebrating symbolic things and events and religious observances. undefined

  • Islamic holidays. Their dates are calculated according to the lunar calendar which makes the incremental changes each year. The significant Muslim holidays celebrated in UAE include Ramadan falls which signifies the end of fasting in the holy month. Also, Eid al-Adha which marks the sacrifice of Prophet Abraham, and Islamic New Year.
  • National holidays. These holidays celebrate the UAEs foundation and heritage. These holidays are:

National Day, on December 2nd, which is a representation of unity of the emirates. Commemoration Day which is on 30th of November, commemorates the UAEs martyrs. In addition to it, Accession Day, that follows on December 2nd, commemorates the day of succession to power of Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Emir of Sheikh Khalifa.

Unpaid Leaves 

In the United Arab Emirates, people working under the umbrella of UAE Labour Law are grant with a type of leave with pay.. Such as sick leave, pregnancy leave, maternity leave, among others. On the contrary, the law gives some consent for unpaid leave.

Employees may apply for unpaid leave. Since this does not fall under the range of their employment contract, the staff member still needs his/her employers agreement. Hence, two sides must sort out the conditions of the leave, including its running time and whether the employee will remain at their place after return back.

Employers have no lawful obligation to grant employees with unpaid leaves of absence. Thus, may, at their sole discretion, either approve or deny such requests. It is essential to note that any unpaid leave taken from work without permission can entail certain consequences, including disciplinary action and even the dismissal of an employee.

Study Leave

Unpaid study leave for the employees is not yet governed by the current UAE labor law. As a result, employers will have the option to choose whether or not to provide unpaid education leave.

Employers in the UAE might provide unpaid study leave as one of the benefits of job. In such cases, the terms and conditions, including the length of the leave and the approval process, would be adopted by the company as per its policies.

For you to take study leave unpaid, it is advisable that you discuss the request with your employer for him to make a decision. They will detail their policy regarding unpaid leave, gauge if they are able to accommodate your needs.

Other Considerations

In addition to the mandated annual leave in UAE, here are some other important considerations regarding leaves in this nation:

  • Await approval. Your manager will review your leave request and make a decision. They may approve your request, request adjustments to the dates, or deny your request due to workload or other factors.

Remember to inform your colleagues and delegate any outstanding tasks before your leave begins.

Check Your Contract and Company Policy

To determine your exact annual leave in UAE, it is advisable that you consult two key documents:

  • Your employment contract. This section should provide the definite details of your paid leave allowance. Such as the number of days that are per year, accrual rate and any further information that could limit your employer such as time restrictions.
  • Company policy documents. It is possible that your organization implements an additional leave policy document which may outline further procedures of leave taking. This include specific agenda for requesting leave, blackout periods, or however many days of leave in any given year..

Therefore, before applying for annual leaves, you have to thoroughly review the contract and company policy documents. This will definitely help you to understand fully what your annual leave rights are and avoid any future fiascos.

How To Plan Your Leave Dates?

Gather Information:

  • First, see to it whether you are eligible for leave in your company.

Consider Public Holidays:

  • Second, look up the official UAE public holiday calendar for 2025. Take advantage of long weekends is a smart way to organize your vacation in order to spend more time away.

Communicate Effectively:

  • After creating a preliminary plan, you should talk with your boss regarding the dates for your leave at an early stage. Explain the reasons and indicate that presence is not crucial for the projects that are of the highest importance.
  • Make sure you communication is lucid, if you want the approval of your favorite leave timing.

How To Submit Your Leave Request?

To request your annual leave in UAE, follow these steps:

  • Send a letter to the manager from your side. First, you need to indicate the precise dates you like to be on leave. Which is part of annual leave proposal.
  • Make your request ahead of time. This is especially relevant during the rush hours, as it helps your leader make the suitable staffing appointments.
  • Look forward for, a confirmation from your manager. Having provided you with a leave approval request, you will receive the confirmation mail. Now it is time for you to reward yourself after hard work.

Approval Process

Obtaining of annual leave approvals from the UAE has not been a problem, as the process is simple.

  • Firstly, the employees have to submit their leave applications with some precaution like the advance of 15 days is compulsory. You can do this either through an office portal or by explicitly telling directly the supervisor.
  • Moreover, some firms might possibly demand employees to indicate the reason behind their trip.
  • Once submitted, the line manager carefully examines the request application and propose solution that accommodates factors like workload and staffing needs before granting.
  • Ultimately, it is crucial for employees to schedule their shifts ahead of time. This is to assure fairness in schedules and to enable smooth continuation of work by their co-workers.

Confirmation and Documentation

Confirmation:

  • Employees in the UAE have an annual leave right, according to law. The contract specifies the exact number of leave days. After the leave application is confirm by the employer, a written notice is also request. The notification should indicate the leave period including the begining and the end dates.

Documentation:

  • In fact, there are no specific or necessary documents to ask for annual leave.
  • This is because some companies have their internal policies for this intention which include submitting additional documents. Such forms could involve a leave request, a flight schedule for an overseas trip, or an invitation for a planned event.
  • It is advisable that you confer with your manager or the Human Resource department. This is to confirm whether they have any additional requirements regarding the documentation.

Subject: Annual Leave Request – [Your Name]

Dear [Managers Name],

I would like to spend my vacation time from [Start Date] until [End Date]. For this purpose I would like to submit a request for a leave of absence for these dates.

In complete, I would concretely use [Number] days for my working days leave. I researched the policy in place at the company and I know I still have leave quota that provides for this absence.

Prior to beginning my leave, I will ensure that I complete my immediate tasks and assign a colleague with the ongoing projects and tasks that I am in charge of.

Beforehand, thank you for taking the time to look over my application. I hope to receive your feedback as well.

Sincerely,

To sum up, the annual leave in UAE is a considerable element of work using employees well-deserved time to relax. The required minimum of 1 month annually makes certain a healthy and balanced work-life equilibrium plus motivate worker productivity.

Furthermore extra leave allocations based upon elements like seniority together with individual scenarios give higher versatility as well as assistance staff member well-being.

What is annual leave as per the UAE Labour Law?

Under the UAE labour law, the annual leave is paid time off that employees earn annually. The leaves start at 2 days per month and 30 days after one year.

Are annual leave days based on calendar days or working days?

As per the UAE labour law, annual leave is calculated in calendar days, not working days.

Do public holidays count during annual leave?

Absolutely not. Public holidays don’t count and are added separately to the employee’s annual leave period.

title: Working Hours in UAE 2025: Stay Compliant & Informed

Working Hours In UAE 2025: Know Your Schedule & Thrive!

Knowing the correct working hours in the UAE isn’t just helpful – it’s essential for both employers and employees.

For private sector employees, the maximum is 8 hours per day (48 hours per week), while public sector employees work 7 hours per day. Understanding these limits helps employers create compliant schedules and allows employees to protect their rights.

This guide explains everything you need to know: standard working hours, Ramadan reductions, overtime rules, flexible work arrangements, and legal protections – so you can stay informed and avoid any penalties.

Standard Working Hours In UAE

 

Employers must ensure that working hours comply with UAE Labour Law, providing safe and fair schedules for employees. Likewise, employees should be aware of their rights to avoid violations related to overtime, multiple employers, or reduced working hours.

Category Private Sector Public Sector
Standard Working Hours 8 hours/day (48 hours/week) 7 hours/day (35 hours/week)
Overtime Limit Up to 2 hours/day Up to 2 hours/day
Ramadan Working Hours Reduced by 2 hours/day Reduced by 2 hours/day
Overtime Pay (Normal) Basic wage + 25% Basic wage + 25%
Overtime Pay (Night Shift) Basic wage + 50% (10 PM – 4 AM) Basic wage + 50% (10 PM – 4 AM)
Midday Break (Summer) Prohibited from 12:30 PM to 3:00 PM (June 15 – September 15) Prohibited from 12:30 PM to 3:00 PM (June 15 – September 15)

 

For Public Sector

If you belong to the public sector, the time required to work must be seven hours a day. Employees of federal government entities follow a four-and-a-half-day workweek. Saturdays and Sundays are the official weekends for the federal administration sector.

For Private Sector

According to Article 65 of the Labor Law, employees and companies belonging to the working hours in UAE for the private sector must work eight hours per day, or 48 hours per week. The standard working day for the private sector is eight hours per day or forty-eight hours per week, according to new working hours in UAE.

You Can Also Check Out: Emergency Leave as Per UAE Labour Law

What Is Flexible Working Arrangements in The UAE

The UAE Labour Law allows for flexible working arrangements, giving employees and employers the option to adapt schedules to meet business needs and personal circumstances. Employees can work part-time, remotely, or split their hours, as long as the total weekly hours do not exceed the legal maximum.

Working Hours for Pregnant Women & Legal Protections in the UAE

Pregnant employees are legally protected under UAE Labour Law to ensure safety and well-being. Key points include:

  • Standard Working Hours: Pregnant employees may continue their usual work hours if it is safe for them.
  • Safety First: Employers must provide a safe working environment and reasonable accommodations.
  • Leave Protections: Maternity leave and related protections apply as per Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 (MOHRE).
  • Reasonable Adjustments: Employers may adjust duties or hours to prevent health risks during pregnancy.
  • Employee Rights: Pregnant employees cannot be forced into overtime or unsafe work.

See More: Maternity Leave In UAE 2025 – An Ultimate Guide

Overtime Calculation And Employee Rights in the UAE

In the UAE, overtime applies when an employee works beyond standard working hours. The law ensures fair compensation and sets limits.

Step-by-Step Overtime Calculation

  1. Identify Standard Working Hours
    • Private sector: 8 hours/day, 48 hours/week
    • Public sector: 7 hours/day, 35 hours/week
  2. Determine Overtime Hours
    • Any work beyond these standard hours counts as overtime.
    • Maximum overtime allowed: 2 hours/day
  3. Calculate Overtime Pay
    • Normal Hours (Daytime): Hourly wage + 25%
    • Night Hours (10 PM – 4 AM): Hourly wage + 50%
  4. Check Special Rules
    • Employees on shifts may have different rules.

Example Calculation

Employee Type Hourly Rate Hours Worked Overtime Hours Overtime Pay Calculation Total Pay
Private Sector Staff AED 50 10 2 2 × 50 × 1.25 = AED 125 Regular pay + AED 125
Night Shift Employee AED 50 2 2 2 × 50 × 1.50 = AED 150 Regular pay + AED 150

Conclusion

Knowing the working hours in UAE is crucial for both employers and employees to maintain compliance and protect rights. The law sets clear rules on standard hours, overtime, Ramadan reductions, and protections for pregnant staff. Flexible arrangements and proper scheduling help businesses operate efficiently while ensuring employee well-being. Staying updated on these regulations and seeking expert guidance when needed ensures a legally compliant and productive workplace for everyone.

Are Working Hours Reduced During Ramadan in UAE?

Yes. During Ramadan, the working hours for all employees are reduced by 2 hours per day as per UAE Labour Law, to accommodate fasting and religious observance.

How Is Overtime Calculated in UAE?

Overtime is calculated for any hours worked beyond standard working hours. Daytime overtime is paid at the regular hourly rate plus 25%, while night shift overtime (10 PM – 4 AM) is paid at the regular rate plus 50%. Maximum overtime is 2 hours per day.

Can Employees Have Flexible Working Hours in UAE?

Yes. UAE Labour Law allows flexible working arrangements, including part-time work, remote work, and split shifts, as long as the total weekly hours do not exceed the legal maximum.

Are Pregnant Women Entitled to Special Working Hour Protections in UAE?

Yes. Pregnant employees are legally protected. They may continue to work their standard hours if it’s safe, but employers must consider health, safety, and reasonable accommodations for pregnant staff.

You can refer to government reports, HR surveys, or trusted industry sources to know the average salary in UAE. This helps in planning fair pay for overtime and complying with labour laws.

title: How Employee Benefits in UAE Boost Engagement
content:
Your Guide on Employee Benefits in the UAE

As of 2025, around 88% of the UAE’s workforce is expats. And while this makes the workplaces diverse with knowledge and skillset, it also brings up an important point: understanding employee benefits and leave entitlements is necessary for knowing your rights.

UAE labour law, specifically Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, goes far more into detail about how compensation, leave, health coverage, and gratuity work.

Understanding Employee Benefits in the UAE

Employee benefits in the UAE are a mix of rights, legal entitlements, and incentives. In a market as competitive as UAE’s, offering fair and comprehensive benefits builds loyalty and boosts productivity among your staff.

Mandatory vs. Non-Mandatory Benefits

Under employee benefits UAE regulations, mandatory benefits include essentials like annual leave, health insurance, and end-of-service gratuity. These are non-negotiable under UAE labour law.

Supplementary or non-mandatory benefits, on the other hand, are where employers can shine by offering bonuses, flexible work, or relocation support to stand out in hiring and retention.

Why Benefits Matter for Both Employers and Employees

For employers, benefits reinforce a positive reputation and keep turnover low. For employees, they’re a sign of value and respect. The right balance makes both sides win: compliance for employers, stability for employees.

Mandatory Employee Benefits as per UAE Labour Law

Every employee in the UAE is entitled to certain statutory benefits. These form the foundation of fair employment, safeguarding both employers’ and employees’ interests.

Salary and Payroll Cycle

Under Article 27 of the Labour Law, employees must be paid at least once a month through the Wage Protection System (WPS).

While there’s no federal minimum wage for expats, Emiratis have structured pay floors based on qualification levels. Employers should ensure prompt and transparent payments to avoid disputes and maintain trust.

Working Hours and Overtime

According to working hours in UAE guidelines, standard hours are capped at 8 per day or 48 per week.

Employees who work beyond this are entitled to overtime: 125% pay for regular overtime and 150% for work at night or on public holidays.

Health Insurance Coverage

Health coverage isn’t optional. Employers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi must provide valid insurance to every employee.

Dependents aren’t included under this obligation, but some employers extend it as part of premium packages. Without valid health insurance, an employee’s visa can face suspension, and employers can be fined.

End of Service Gratuity (EOSB)

Often the most anticipated part of employee benefits in UAE, gratuity acts as a retirement cushion.

Employees completing one year or more of service earn 21 days of basic pay per year for the first five years and 30 days thereafter, capped at two years’ salary.

Types of Leaves in the UAE

Work-life balance is upheld by the law as well. UAE’s labour law defines several types of leaves in UAE to help employees recharge, recover, and handle personal matters responsibly.

Annual Leave in the UAE

Under annual leave in UAE, employees who complete one year of service are entitled to 30 calendar days of paid leave. Those with six months to a year get two days per month. Employers must pay leave salary before the leave begins.

Sick Leaves in the UAE

For sick leave in UAE, employees with at least three months of continuous service qualify for up to 90 days per year: 15 with full pay, 30 with half pay, and 45 unpaid.

This directly answers your question of ‘how many medical leaves per year in UAE?’ Exactly 90 days with a valid medical certificate being required.

Maternity Leaves in the UAE

Under maternity leave in UAE rules, female employees get 60 days of leave: 45 with full pay and 15 with half pay. They have the option for another 45 unpaid days for medical reasons.

Paternity and Parental Leave

New parents, both mothers and fathers, get 5 days of paternity leave in UAE within six months of childbirth. These can be taken consecutively or split across days.

Compassionate (Bereavement) Leave

Employees can take bereavement leave in UAE: five days for a spouse’s death, three for a close family member.

Study Leave and Sabbatical Leave in UAE

Employees pursuing education in UAE-certified institutions get 10 days per year for exams after two years of service.

Sabbatical leave in UAE for expats doesn’t apply. But UAE nationals are eligible for it if they are serving in national programs.

Public Holidays and Eid Leaves in UAE

Employees enjoy all national holidays declared by the UAE government. These are usually about 14 days a year, covering Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, National Day, and more.

Additional Employee Benefits and Allowances in the UAE

In a market full of competitive employers, going beyond the law can be a dealbreaker or a dealmaker. Supplemental benefits can give you the edge as an employer.

Performance Bonuses and Allowances

Many companies offer housing, transport, and travel allowances or bonuses tied to performance goals. These perks motivate employees and show recognition beyond the monthly paycheck.

Pension and Social Security Contributions

For UAE nationals and GCC citizens, employers contribute 12.5% toward pensions, while employees contribute 5%, and the government adds 2.5%. It is managed by the General Pension and Social Security Authority (GPSSA).

Repatriation Ticket

When a contract ends, the employer should cover the cost of returning the employee to their home country unless they have already joined another employer.

How Employee Benefits Impact Engagement and Retention

When people feel valued, they stay. That’s the simplest summary of how UAE employee benefits affect engagement.

Financial and Emotional Security

Health insurance, fair pay, and gratuity go beyond financial comfort. These build trust too. Employees who feel secure are more productive and loyal.

Work-Life Balance

Balanced leave policies show employers care about life beyond work. It not only gives you a chance at rest, but also the opportunity for a mental reset. 

Attraction of Top Talent

Companies offering competitive packages attract top candidates faster. With transparent UAE employee benefits calculator tools, job seekers can easily compare offers, making transparency even more vital.

How Employers Can Stay Compliant with UAE Labour Law

Ignoring benefit obligations leads to legal consequences. From fines to suspension of work permits, compliance matters.

Maintain Transparent Contracts

Outline all salary, benefits, and leave entitlements clearly in employment contracts. It prevents disputes and builds confidence.

Regularly Review MOHRE Updates

Laws tend to change and update. Stay current with updates from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) to meet the latest requirements on benefits of terminated employees in UAE and avoid any lapses.

Conclusion

Understanding employee benefits as per UAE labour law empowers you to create workplaces that reward, protect, and empower your workforce.

Employers who invest in well-being and compliance enjoy stronger teams and fewer legal hassles. And employees who understand their rights can make informed career decisions confidently.

At RAAD Recruitment, we help businesses optimize their compensation and benefits strategy to attract and retain top talent while staying compliant with UAE’s labour law.

Get in touch with us to learn more about how our Emiratisation services support compliance and national hiring goals.

FAQs

What Are the Mandatory Employee Benefits in The UAE?

They include annual leave, health insurance, public holidays, end-of-service gratuity, and paid sick leave as defined by UAE Labour Law.

How to Calculate Benefits in UAE?

Use a UAE employee benefits calculator or consult MOHRE for formulas that account for tenure, basic pay, and unused leave days.

Do Expats Get Gratuity Benefits in The UAE?

Yes, gratuity applies to both UAE nationals and expatriates who complete at least one year of continuous service.

Are Employers Required to Provide Health Insurance to Employees?

Yes, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, employers must provide valid health insurance coverage for every employee.

How Much Gratuity After 1 Year in UAE?

After one year, employees are entitled to 21 days of basic pay per completed year of service, as part of the gratuity and employee benefits program UAE.

For employers, benefits reinforce a positive reputation and keep turnover low. For employees, they’re a sign of value and respect. The right balance makes both sides win: compliance for employers, stability for employees.

Mandatory Employee Benefits as per UAE Labour Law

Every employee in the UAE is entitled to certain statutory benefits. These form the foundation of fair employment, safeguarding both employers’ and employees’ interests.

Salary and Payroll Cycle

Under Article 27 of the Labour Law, employees must be paid at least once a month through the Wage Protection System (WPS).

While there’s no federal minimum wage for expats, Emiratis have structured pay floors based on qualification levels. Employers should ensure prompt and transparent payments to avoid disputes and maintain trust.

Working Hours and Overtime

According to working hours in UAE guidelines, standard hours are capped at 8 per day or 48 per week.

Employees who work beyond this are entitled to overtime: 125% pay for regular overtime and 150% for work at night or on public holidays.

Health Insurance Coverage

Health coverage isn’t optional. Employers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi must provide valid insurance to every employee.

Dependents aren’t included under this obligation, but some employers extend it as part of premium packages. Without valid health insurance, an employee’s visa can face suspension, and employers can be fined.

End of Service Gratuity (EOSB)

Often the most anticipated part of employee benefits in UAE, gratuity acts as a retirement cushion.

Employees completing one year or more of service earn 21 days of basic pay per year for the first five years and 30 days thereafter, capped at two years’ salary.

Types of Leaves in the UAE

Work-life balance is upheld by the law as well. UAE’s labour law defines several types of leaves in UAE to help employees recharge, recover, and handle personal matters responsibly.

Annual Leave in the UAE

Under annual leave in UAE, employees who complete one year of service are entitled to 30 calendar days of paid leave. Those with six months to a year get two days per month. Employers must pay leave salary before the leave begins.

Sick Leaves in the UAE

For sick leave in UAE, employees with at least three months of continuous service qualify for up to 90 days per year: 15 with full pay, 30 with half pay, and 45 unpaid.

This directly answers your question of ‘how many medical leaves per year in UAE?’ Exactly 90 days with a valid medical certificate being required.

Maternity Leaves in the UAE

Under maternity leave in UAE rules, female employees get 60 days of leave: 45 with full pay and 15 with half pay. They have the option for another 45 unpaid days for medical reasons.

Paternity and Parental Leave

New parents, both mothers and fathers, get 5 days of paternity leave in UAE within six months of childbirth. These can be taken consecutively or split across days.

Compassionate (Bereavement) Leave

Employees can take bereavement leave in UAE: five days for a spouse’s death, three for a close family member.

Study Leave and Sabbatical Leave in UAE

Employees pursuing education in UAE-certified institutions get 10 days per year for exams after two years of service.

Sabbatical leave in UAE for expats doesn’t apply. But UAE nationals are eligible for it if they are serving in national programs.

Public Holidays and Eid Leaves in UAE

Employees enjoy all national holidays declared by the UAE government. These are usually about 14 days a year, covering Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, National Day, and more.

Additional Employee Benefits and Allowances in the UAE

In a market full of competitive employers, going beyond the law can be a dealbreaker or a dealmaker. Supplemental benefits can give you the edge as an employer.

Performance Bonuses and Allowances

Many companies offer housing, transport, and travel allowances or bonuses tied to performance goals. These perks motivate employees and show recognition beyond the monthly paycheck.

Pension and Social Security Contributions

For UAE nationals and GCC citizens, employers contribute 12.5% toward pensions, while employees contribute 5%, and the government adds 2.5%. It is managed by the General Pension and Social Security Authority (GPSSA).

Repatriation Ticket

When a contract ends, the employer should cover the cost of returning the employee to their home country unless they have already joined another employer.

How Employee Benefits Impact Engagement and Retention

When people feel valued, they stay. That’s the simplest summary of how UAE employee benefits affect engagement.

Financial and Emotional Security

Health insurance, fair pay, and gratuity go beyond financial comfort. These build trust too. Employees who feel secure are more productive and loyal.

Work-Life Balance

Balanced leave policies show employers care about life beyond work. It not only gives you a chance at rest, but also the opportunity for a mental reset. 

Attraction of Top Talent

Companies offering competitive packages attract top candidates faster. With transparent UAE employee benefits calculator tools, job seekers can easily compare offers, making transparency even more vital.

How Employers Can Stay Compliant with UAE Labour Law

Ignoring benefit obligations leads to legal consequences. From fines to suspension of work permits, compliance matters.

Maintain Transparent Contracts

Outline all salary, benefits, and leave entitlements clearly in employment contracts. It prevents disputes and builds confidence.

Regularly Review MOHRE Updates

Laws tend to change and update. Stay current with updates from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) to meet the latest requirements on benefits of terminated employees in UAE and avoid any lapses.

Conclusion

Understanding employee benefits as per UAE labour law empowers you to create workplaces that reward, protect, and empower your workforce.

Employers who invest in well-being and compliance enjoy stronger teams and fewer legal hassles. And employees who understand their rights can make informed career decisions confidently.

At RAAD Recruitment, we help businesses optimize their compensation and benefits strategy to attract and retain top talent while staying compliant with UAE’s labour law.

Get in touch with us to learn more about how our Emiratisation services support compliance and national hiring goals.

FAQs

What Are the Mandatory Employee Benefits in The UAE?

They include annual leave, health insurance, public holidays, end-of-service gratuity, and paid sick leave as defined by UAE Labour Law.

How to Calculate Benefits in UAE?

Use a UAE employee benefits calculator or consult MOHRE for formulas that account for tenure, basic pay, and unused leave days.

Do Expats Get Gratuity Benefits in The UAE?

Yes, gratuity applies to both UAE nationals and expatriates who complete at least one year of continuous service.

Are Employers Required to Provide Health Insurance to Employees?

Yes, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, employers must provide valid health insurance coverage for every employee.

How Much Gratuity After 1 Year in UAE?

After one year, employees are entitled to 21 days of basic pay per completed year of service, as part of the gratuity and employee benefits program UAE.

Maternity Leave In UAE 2025– Get Paid & Pampered in the UAE

Having a baby can be an amazing experience. However, working mothers should consider maternity Leave in UAE. This provides income and job security for working mothers at a critical stage in their lives. In the United Arab Emirates, maternity leave is a labor right granted only to pregnant women.

In this article, we will analyze maternity leave in the UAE to show you the requirements, exceptions, and benefits. We will also show you who is eligible for maternity leave in UAE and some of the features you can access with this maternity leave in UAE for government employees. Finally, here are some practical tips to help you manage your work and family during this special time.

What Is Maternity Leave In UAE?

Maternity Leave in UAE, also known as paternity leave in UAE, allows an employee to leave the workplace. They can use this time to care for their newborn and themselves. Companies often compensate for this time off to help mothers recover from childbirth and bond with their babies. Therefore, there are several maternity leave guidelines for employers to follow.

Therefore, if you want to have children in the UAE and you are a worker, you should ensure that your rights are respected. This allows you to enjoy the benefits of working in the UAE. However, in terms of leave, UAE labor laws have changed. Therefore, maternity leave is longer compared to that of private sector workers.

Also, employees of UAE authorities are entitled to three months of paid maternity leave from the date of birth. However, you can apply for maternity Leave in UAE up to 30 days before the expected date of birth.

Benefits for Women Under UAE Labour Law

This approach offers several benefits for both mother and child. Research on paid maternity policies shows that these measures contribute to significant reductions in infant mortality. It also helps to improve the overall health of your child. So, for more information on maternity leave benefits in the United Arab Emirates can be found here.

1. Paid Leave

During maternity leave, female employees are entitled to receive full salary for the first 45 days and half pay for the remaining 15 days. This compensation is provided by the company and is not deducted from the employee’s accrued leave balance. This ensures that mothers can focus on their health and well-being without facing financial stress.

2. Additional Leave

The previous labor legislation regulates in Article 30 the cases in which a working mother may need to be absent from work due to health-related complications, allowing 100 additional days of unpaid leave, provided they are requested with the necessary medical certificates.

3. Job Security

Maternity leave in the UAE enables employees to strike a balance between both their private and professional lives.

Also, companies that offer generous maternity leave policies in the UAE tend to be more attractive to job applicants. In other words, it is a company with a high level of employee stability. Employees are much more likely to stay with companies that support them during critical life events.

Besides, all female employees who are able to take maternity leave in the UAE are more likely to return to work with a positive attitude. They also have higher job satisfaction.

4. Nursing Rights

As well, on the weekend, female employees are entitled to breastfeeding breaks, provided they comply with the following rules:

  • Female employees are entitled to a breastfeeding break of two days for six months from the date of birth. Each break must not exceed 30 minutes. During this period, employees are entitled to their full salary.
  • However, the working hours of pregnant women in the UAE will not change unless they are sick or have agreed with the company.
  • Also, regardless of the classification of a private company, it must comply with the provisions of the law.
  • Therefore, since there are many benefits a company has to offer its employees, it is important to know the true cost of being an employee.

5. Access to Daycare Facilities

It is a common challenge faced by working mothers around the world to balance work and family responsibilities, and the UAE is no exception. Long working hours and a demanding work culture can make it difficult for mothers to find a healthy work-life balance.

That is why, maternity leave in UAE companies offer flexible working arrangements, such as part-time or telecommuting, to access the needs of new mothers and facilitate their re-entry into the labor market.

How Many Days Maternity Leave in UAE for Private Sector

Women working in the private sector in the UAE are also entitled to maternity Leave in UAE. However, the period of parental leave in the private sector is different from that in the public sector. Also, according to the new maternity leave in UAE labor law, pregnant women in the private sector have the following entitlements:

The 60 days of maternity leave is divided as follows:

  • 45 days paid maternity leave.
  • Extended leave of 15 days with partial pay.

If supporting documents are submitted, an additional 45 days of unpaid leave is granted if the mother or child becomes ill. Mothers of children with disabilities receive an additional 30 days of paid leave. You can extend it for 90 days of maternity leave for the private sector without pay, adding to the list of private sector benefits available to working mothers.

Maternity leave in the UAE includes time before and after birth. In addition to maternity leave, women working in the private sector are entitled to breastfeeding leave twice a day for 18 months from the date of birth.

Breastfeeding breaks should not exceed 30 minutes at a time. During this period, women were entitled to their full salary. UAE labor law allows men working in the private sector to take five days of paternity leave. In the UAE, parental leave can be taken at any time up to 6 months after the birth.

Also Recommended: Emergency Leave in UAE Labour Law

Eligibility Criteria For Maternity Leaves

To be eligible for maternity leave in the UAE, an employee must have worked continuously for at least one year in the company. Even if employees have not worked for one year, they are entitled to take unpaid leave to care for their children.

1. Employment Status

The worker must be in a formal employment relationship with an employer. This means that she must be employed by a legally registered company or entity.

In many countries, the worker must meet certain minimum terms of employment before she is eligible for maternity leave. For example, she must have worked for a specified period (e.g., 6 months or 1 year) before the expected date of childbirth.

2. Pregnancy Proof

Generally, to be eligible for maternity leave, the worker must have a confirmed pregnancy. This is verified by a medical certificate or pregnancy test.

3. Notification

The worker generally must notify her employer of her pregnancy and her intention to take maternity leave. This is done in advance so that the employer can make the necessary arrangements.

Duration of Maternity Leaves in the UAE

If you want to know how long is maternity leave in UAE, female employees are entitled to 45 days of maternity leave and an additional 15 days of pay leave. If an employee has difficulties at work, he/she may choose to take an additional 15 days of paid leave. Employees may start maternity leave up to 30 days before the expected date of birth.

If the child is sick or disabled, the mother is entitled to 30 days of paid leave and another 30 days of unpay leave. Only a medical certificate from an accredited medical institution is required.

In 2019, the UAE Cabinet introduced reforms to the labor legislation. Through this reform, maternity leave is extended from 45 days to 90 days. This also includes unpaid or combined leave, including annual leave or sick leave. The latest UAE labor laws apply to all UAE women workers employed in the government or private sector.

Legal Protections and Rights for Pregnant Employees

  • The maternity test will be counted only if medical reports and health certificates are submitted.
  • According to the UAE embassy enforcement data, it has been mandatory to apply a pension system for mothers during the 45-day period.
  • A health report of the newborn is required to check whether the newborn is alive or dead.
  • If some female employees enroll in their position during the employee’s maternity leave, then they can only work during that time until the employee returns from her maternity duration.
  • If the woman appeals the maternity leave, the company cannot oppose or cancel the employee’s candidacy.
  • No hiring and no formalities can be carried out.
  • Female employees are allowed to take initial leave and private leave.
  • Only present the original of the health copy records to the maternal period to the company’s companies.

How many days of maternity leave are women entitled to in the UAE in 2025?

In 2025, UAE female employees will get 60 calendar days of maternity leave. This shall be granted under the UAE Labour Law.

Who is eligible for maternity leave in the UAE?

Any female employee is eligible for maternity leave in the UAE. It must be subject to having a valid employment contract under the UAE Labour Law.

Do female employees receive full salary during maternity leave in the UAE?

Yes! Employees will receive a full salary for the first 45 days. The remaining leaves will get them half pay per law.

Can maternity leave be extended in the UAE?

Extensions depend on various factors. This may include:

  • Medical conditions
  • Employer agreement or
  • Special circumstances

Can an employer terminate a woman during maternity leave?

No! Termination during maternity leave is prohibited under the UAE Labour Law protections.
